evidence.claim: The World Bank said Nigeria spent only about 220 dollars per person in 2022, social sectors received less than a quarter of the national budget, and low public spending translated into poor development outcomes and weak human capital.
evidence.title: Nigeria's need to spend more and better
evidence.excerpt: The World Bank said Nigeria spent only about 220 dollars per person in 2022, social sectors received less than a quarter of the national budget, and low public spending translated into poor development outcomes and weak human capital.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Primary World Bank feature with clear quantitative claims and policy interpretation.
evidence.period_fit: Directly describes 2022 spending conditions and their welfare implications.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Buhari's administration because it concerns federal public spending choices, though inherited fiscal constraints also mattered.
contrary_evidence: The page is a policy diagnosis, not a direct audit of Buhari's personal management of each sector.

evidence.claim: Buhari framed the 2022 budget around a vibrant, educated, and healthy populace, poverty reduction, and reduced regional and social disparities, and said MDAs were advised to use gender-responsive budgeting to reach vulnerable groups.
evidence.title: 2022 Budget Speech: Budget of Economic Growth and Sustainability – President Buhari
evidence.excerpt: Buhari framed the 2022 budget around a vibrant, educated, and healthy populace, poverty reduction, and reduced regional and social disparities, and said MDAs were advised to use gender-responsive budgeting to reach vulnerable groups.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official budget speech, but it is an intention-and-priority statement rather than a delivery report.
evidence.period_fit: Pre-2022 fiscal plan that governed the target year.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler attribution for the budget proposal and stated priorities.
contrary_evidence: Budget proposals do not establish actual delivery or beneficiary reach in 2022.

evidence.claim: Buhari signed the National Health Insurance Authority Bill 2022, said a fund would be created to cover 83 million poor Nigerians who cannot afford premiums, and said the new law would support digital records, data collection, and monitoring.
evidence.title: In Bid to Achieve Universal Coverage, President Buhari Signs National Health Authority Bill Into Law
evidence.excerpt: Buhari signed the National Health Insurance Authority Bill 2022, said a fund would be created to cover 83 million poor Nigerians who cannot afford premiums, and said the new law would support digital records, data collection, and monitoring.
evidence.source_locator: opening paragraphs and presidential remarks on the fund and digital records
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official enactment record with explicit institutional and coverage claims.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler action, although actual coverage depended on implementation by the Authority and state schemes.
contrary_evidence: Signing the law did not itself prove that the fund or coverage was fully operational in 2022.

evidence.claim: Buhari said the administration's humanitarian and social-development framework included the National IDP Policy, the National Emergency Flood and Response Plan, policies for the elderly and disability, the poverty-reduction plan, and social-investment programmes such as school feeding, conditional cash transfers, N-Power, and GEEP.
evidence.title: Humanitarian Issues: President Buhari Urges More Private Sector Participation, Highlights Intervention Programmes
evidence.excerpt: Buhari said the administration's humanitarian and social-development framework included the National IDP Policy, the National Emergency Flood and Response Plan, policies for the elderly and disability, the poverty-reduction plan, and social-investment programmes such as school feeding, conditional cash transfers, N-Power, and GEEP.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct official speech, but it is primarily self-reported policy framing and program enumeration.
evidence.period_fit: Direct 2022 statement of welfare strategy and target groups.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Direct ruler attribution for the administration's program agenda.
contrary_evidence: The speech lists programs and goals but does not independently demonstrate national-scale impact.

evidence.claim: Buhari directed ministries and agencies to develop programmes for explosive remnants, orphaned children, and return and rehabilitation of internally displaced people in the North East, and linked the directive to reducing the effects of insurgency and disaster.
evidence.title: President Buhari Directs Humanitarian Affairs Ministry, Others to Ensure Unimpeded Return of IDPs in the North east
evidence.excerpt: Buhari directed ministries and agencies to develop programmes for explosive remnants, orphaned children, and return and rehabilitation of internally displaced people in the North East, and linked the directive to reducing the effects of insurgency and disaster.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Direct target-year directive, but still a presidential instruction rather than proof of full delivery.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly attributable to Buhari's crisis-response authority, though implementation depended on ministries, states, and security conditions.
contrary_evidence: The underlying displacement and insurgency were inherited and not eliminated by this directive.

evidence.claim: The evaluation found that the UN-government social-protection programme alleviated recipients' financial burdens, encouraged them to seek professional health care, helped meet immediate needs, and strengthened coordination among government social-protection stakeholders.
evidence.title: Nigeria, Joint Evaluation of Social Protection for SDGs in Nigeria Project
evidence.excerpt: The evaluation found that the UN-government social-protection programme alleviated recipients' financial burdens, encouraged them to seek professional health care, helped meet immediate needs, and strengthened coordination among government social-protection stakeholders.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Official evaluation summary of a joint UN-government programme with explicit outcome statements.
evidence.period_fit: Covers January 2020 to June 2022, overlapping the target year and ending during Buhari's tenure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Buhari's administration because it concerns a national social-protection programme, though implementation was joint with UN agencies and states.
contrary_evidence: The evaluation is joint and does not isolate Buhari's personal contribution from partner agencies.

evidence.claim: Reuters reported that an eight-month university lecturers' strike kept students out of classrooms, that the union suspended the strike in deference to presidential appeals, and that Buhari had said the government was dismayed and set aside 470 billion naira for salary enhancements in tertiary institutions.
evidence.title: Nigeria's public university lecturers suspend strike after eight months
evidence.excerpt: Reuters reported that an eight-month university lecturers' strike kept students out of classrooms, that the union suspended the strike in deference to presidential appeals, and that Buhari had said the government was dismayed and set aside 470 billion naira for salary enhancements in tertiary institutions.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: Contemporaneous Reuters reporting syndicated by Euronews, but still reporting a contentious labor dispute rather than a clean implementation record.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Directly relevant to Buhari because he appealed to end the strike and his budget response is cited, though the dispute also involved the union and universities.
contrary_evidence: The union said the issues were not yet satisfactorily addressed, so the settlement remained incomplete.

evidence.claim: UNICEF reported that cash grants helped return 300,000 pupils to school, including girls in Katsina, and that schools used grants for boreholes, toilets, classrooms, and learning materials while hundreds of girls were brought back into education.
evidence.title: In north-west Nigeria, cash grants take out-of-school children back to school
evidence.excerpt: UNICEF reported that cash grants helped return 300,000 pupils to school, including girls in Katsina, and that schools used grants for boreholes, toilets, classrooms, and learning materials while hundreds of girls were brought back into education.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: UNICEF story with concrete program outcomes and beneficiary testimony from 2022.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to the broader Nigerian social-protection and education environment, but the program was implemented with UNICEF and local partners, not by Buhari alone.
contrary_evidence: The story also says many children in the area remained out of school, so gains were partial and localized.

evidence.claim: WHO reported that Nigeria ranked first among zero-dose countries in 2022 with over 2.3 million estimated zero-dose children, that the government prioritized reaching these communities in its national immunization and PHC strategy, and that data-targeted collaboration helped reach millions of children with immunization services.
evidence.title: Strong collaboration for better health: Closing immunization gaps in Nigeria through a primary health care approach
evidence.excerpt: WHO reported that Nigeria ranked first among zero-dose countries in 2022 with over 2.3 million estimated zero-dose children, that the government prioritized reaching these communities in its national immunization and PHC strategy, and that data-targeted collaboration helped reach millions of children with immunization services.
evidence.source_confidence_reason: WHO results-report country story with target-year estimates and explicit system responses, albeit published retrospectively.
evidence.period_fit: Retrospectively describes 2022 health-access conditions and the 2020-2023 response period overlapping Buhari's tenure.
evidence.ruler_attribution: Partly attributable to Buhari's administration through national strategy and PHC system oversight, but implementation was shared with WHO, UNICEF, and subnational actors.
contrary_evidence: The same source shows a very large remaining immunization gap, so progress was incomplete.

unresolved_gaps: No direct 2022 Buhari decision on nuclear brinkmanship, command-and-control, or other existential-risk use of presidential authority.
No independent audit of whether the 2021-2022 safeguards and physical-protection framework was actually implemented in practice.
No direct evidence of Buhari personally directing external military operations, proxy conduct, or coercive cross-border action in 2022.
No substantive mediation track or concrete ceasefire result led by Buhari himself.
Independent, case-level follow-through on prosecutions and investigations for major 2022 abuses is thin.
Some severe insecurity items are still better understood as state failure in a violent environment than as direct ruler-directed violence.
No independent pre-election audit of how fully the Electoral Act 2022 was implemented before the 2023 polls.
Much of the affirmative evidence is self-description from Buhari and his administration.
Budget execution and capital-spending delivery are not independently audited at the project level here.
Household-level and regional distributional causality remains only partially evidenced.
Independent audit evidence on how much of the announced welfare and health delivery actually reached beneficiaries in 2022 is limited.
The chapter still mixes federal action, donor support, and inherited deprivation.
No direct 2022 evidence of Buhari's assets, procurement benefits, bribes, or formal audit/court findings tied to personal enrichment.
The family-appointment case is strong on patronage but still thin on Buhari's knowledge, benefit, and intent beyond approval.
The Lake Chad arms claim is shown as unsupported, but there is no public correction or retraction by Buhari in the package.
Independent audit-grade evidence on the delivery tracker and the administration's correction of weak implementers is still limited.
The chapter still depends heavily on macro outcomes that mix Buhari-era policy with inherited constraints and external shocks.
